verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. kind='missing-heading' is factually wrong. The heading is present, verbatim and complete, at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:28547 as '## 14.9.25.4 General rules', immediately preceded by a correct anchor ''. I diffed the whole page-696 work unit against the 300dpi render: Table 16 (all 10 body rows, both Numeric sub-rows), the FORMAT 2 banner, syntax rules 11)-13), the 14.9.25.4 heading, the FORMAT 1 banner, and general rule 1) with all three of its paragraphs are all present and word-for-word correct. Not one glyph of ISO text on this page is absent, altered or added. (2) THE PDF CANNOT SUPPORT THE CLAIMED DISCREPANCY -- this is decisive. I rendered both page 696 (printed 666) and page 694 (printed 664) to inspect the typography directly. ISO prints '14.9.25 MOVE statement', '14.9.25.1 General', '14.9.25.2 General formats', '14.9.25.3 Syntax rules' (all on printed p.664) and '14.9.25.4 General rules' (printed p.666) in the IDENTICAL bold face, at the IDENTICAL type size, flush at the IDENTICAL left margin. ISO/IEC directives style carries clause depth exclusively in the dotted clause NUMBER, never typographically, at these levels. So the claim's stated evidence -- '.4 is printed at the same typographic level as .1/.2/.3' -- is true but vacuous: it is equally true of the PARENT 14.9.25, which is also set in that same face and size. The PDF carries zero information distinguishing an h2 from an h3 here, so no PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy can be derived from it. A reconciliation ledger of the PDF against its transcription has nothing to record. (3) THE UNDERLYING ISSUE IS REAL BUT IS A DOCUMENT-WIDE MARKDOWN CONVENTION INCONSISTENCY, NOT A PAGE-696 EVENT. Tallying every 14.9.x.y heading: 26 clauses render '## ...4 General rules' against 25 that render '### ...4 General rules'; 14 render '## ...3 Syntax rules' against 37 '###'. The transcription has no consistent convention to violate -- it is split near 50/50. 14.9.24.4 (28341), 14.9.25.4 (28547) and 14.9.26.4 (28797) are all '##' while every .1/.2/.3 around them is '###'. Ledgering this per page would generate ~40 near-duplicate structural findings for one systematic artifact; the correct remedy, if any, is a single document-wide normalization pass keyed on the clause number's component count. (4) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES ITS OWN CITATIONS. Every line number is stale by exactly 3: actual 28547 (claimed 28544), 28459 (claimed 28456), 28464 (claimed 28461), 28483 (claimed 28480). The uniform offset indicates the claim was generated against an earlier revision of the file. PRACTICAL IMPACT IS NIL FOR THIS PROJECT. Citations throughout this codebase address the spec by clause number ('14.9.25, MOVE statement, General rule 6'), and the anchor 'section-14-9-25-4' is correct and depth-independent. Both the numeric-citation and the anchor-link navigation paths resolve correctly regardless of the '#' count. Only a consumer that reconstructs hierarchy from '#' depth while ignoring the clause number it is reading would be affected.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. No ISO content is missing from page 696 -- the heading '14.9.25.4 General rules' is present verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:28547 with a correct 'section-14-9-25-4' anchor, and the rest of the page (Table 16, FORMAT 2, rules 11-13, FORMAT 1, rule 1) transcribes faithfully. The claim's PDF evidence does not hold: ISO prints 14.9.25, 14.9.25.1, .2, .3 and .4 in one identical bold face, size and margin, encoding clause depth only in the dotted number, so the PDF distinguishes no heading levels and cannot witness an h2-vs-h3 defect. What genuinely exists is an internal markdown convention inconsistency spanning the whole document -- 26 '## ...4 General rules' vs 25 '### ...4 General rules', and 14 '## ...3 Syntax rules' vs 37 '###' -- which, if it is worth correcting, belongs in one document-wide heading-depth normalization keyed on the clause number's component count, not as a per-page reconciliation finding. The claim additionally cites all four line numbers 3 lines stale (28547/28459/28464/28483, not 28544/28456/28461/28480).
